Before starting: Complete the foundations pack: assignment, types, comparisons, selection and boundary tests. Teach these four activities in order; revisit tracing before adding repetition.

Suggested 55-minute lesson: 8 minutes textbook reading, 12 modelling, 20 independent practice, 10 feedback and 5 exit reflection. Adapt after classroom trial. Keep predictions separate from observed results. Paper traces are valid practice but do not prove that software or equipment ran.

2026 foundation · 2027 revisions. Public, ungraded formative practice; answers are on a separate page. No student responses are collected. Optional specialist equipment can supply a context after the general task; it is not required.

01 · Count and accumulate

Read, predict and model

Name __________________ Class ______ Date __________

Textbook visit: Read the linked chapter. Return to its worked examples before trying the independent task.

A club records points of 2, 4 and 6. range(1, 4) supplies 1, 2, 3; the stop value is excluded. Start total outside the loop so earlier values are preserved.

total = 0
for round_number in range(1, 4):
    total = total + round_number * 2
print(total)
RoundAddedTotal after update
122
246
3612

The loop runs three times and prints 12. Moving total = 0 inside the loop would discard earlier additions.

Equipment-free route

Use a pencil and a trace table, treating each loop iteration as one row. Record hand-traced results explicitly; do not label them as executed Python output.

Explain and transfer

Annotate one step of the worked example in your own words. Change one supplied input, record a new prediction and show how the rule produces it. Label a hand trace separately from a software observation.

02 · Return a result from a function

Read, predict and model

Name __________________ Class ______ Date __________

Textbook visit: Read the linked chapter. Return to its worked examples before trying the independent task.

This function applies a fixed booking charge of $2 and $3 per item. Assume quantity is a non-negative integer. The parameter is local to the function; return sends a value back to its caller.

def booking_cost(quantity):
    return quantity * 3 + 2

first = booking_cost(4)
print(first)

quantity receives 4, the expression evaluates to 14, first receives 14 and print displays it. Defining the function alone does not perform this call.

Equipment-free route

Act out the function with an input card and a separate return card. Calculate all three calls by hand and label the results as traced.

Explain and transfer

Annotate one step of the worked example in your own words. Change one supplied input, record a new prediction and show how the rule produces it. Label a hand trace separately from a software observation.

03 · Traverse a list and retain a position

Read, predict and model

Name __________________ Class ______ Date __________

Textbook visit: Read the linked chapter. Return to its worked examples before trying the independent task.

The task is to find the index of the first smallest value in a non-empty list. Start with the first valid index. Use <, rather than <=, to preserve the first equal minimum.

values = [8, 3, 3, 6]
best = 0
for index in range(1, len(values)):
    if values[index] < values[best]:
        best = index
print(best, values[best])

At index 1 the minimum becomes 3; the equal 3 at index 2 does not replace it. The output is 1 3. The initial index is invalid for an empty list.

Equipment-free route

Cut out value cards and number their positions from zero. Move a best-index marker only when the comparison is true.

Explain and transfer

Annotate one step of the worked example in your own words. Change one supplied input, record a new prediction and show how the rule produces it. Label a hand trace separately from a software observation.

04 · Read a file and test bad records

Read, predict and model

Name __________________ Class ______ Date __________

Textbook visit: Read the linked chapter. Return to its worked examples before trying the independent task.

Assume a UTF-8 text file called readings.txt exists in the working folder. It contains one integer per line. The example ignores blank lines; a non-integer line is reported and skipped. File-not-found recovery is a separate task.

total = 0
with open("readings.txt", encoding="utf-8") as source:
    for line in source:
        text = line.strip()
        if text != "":
            try:
                total += int(text)
            except ValueError:
                print("Invalid:", text)
print("Total:", total)

For lines 3, blank, x, 5 the output is Invalid: x followed by Total: 8. int converts suitable text; the exception branch does not add a value.

Equipment-free route

Use the printed record lines as the file. Trace the accumulator and output queue line by line; no editor or device is required.

Explain and transfer

Annotate one step of the worked example in your own words. Change one supplied input, record a new prediction and show how the rule produces it. Label a hand trace separately from a software observation.
